atoms.a: I don't eat meat anymore for environmental reasons. Livestock use a huge amount of water and land, and they produce a lot of carbon emissions. Also, rainforests are cut down to make way for farming, which destroys the habitats of some endangered species. That's why I try to eat more sustainably now.
b: ++The speaker has stopped eating meat because of the environmental impact.
++Farming can lead to rainforests being cut down.
The speaker still eats meat sometimes, just less often.

instruction.text: Welche Überschrift passt am besten zum Gesagten? Wähle aus.

atoms.a: Last year, our student council decided that something had to be done about how much waste our school was producing. We put recycling bins in every classroom and asked the cafeteria to reduce plastic packaging. We also made sure to switch off the lights in empty classrooms to save on electricity.

Before our family trip to Portugal, my mum showed me a website where we could calculate the amount carbon emissions our flight would produce. I was surprised to learn that the amount was much greater than it would have been if we had chosen to take the train or even drive. Ever since, I've started checking whether trains are a realistic option before booking a flight.

atoms.text: Schreibe die fehlenden Wörter in die Lücken.

instruction.sound: As head teacher, I want to tell you why recycling at school is really important, and how everyone can help. First, waste must be sorted into four different bins. These are paper, plastic, glass, and organic waste. Batteries and electronics mustn't be put into the bins – they must be taken to a special collection point... Then, paper is recycled to save trees, and plastic bottles can be turned into new products instead of ending up in the ocean. Students should always check the label on the bin before throwing something away. If we all do this, less waste will be sent to landfill and our school can set a real example for sustainability. Thank you!
